metas.note:
Utility poles in most of California have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes. Modoc County and Lassen County in the Northeast of the state are the main exceptions.

(This design can also be found in the city of Grants Pass, Oregon.)

metas.name: California - Special Pavement Markers
metas.note:
Rectangular pavement markers each on the side of the double lines are commonly found in Georgia, Florida, Texas, and California. Other rectangular RPM states have the RPM between the double lines.

NOTE: Beware of similar patterns in left turn lanes.

metas.name: Idaho - Square 1 Bolt Bollard
metas.note:
Bollards where the reflector is shaped like a square are common in Utah, Arizona, and Idaho.

Idaho features both styles of this square bollard (1 and 2 bolt) evenly.

NOTE: Diamond bollards can be rotated on their side to look like squares. Use with caution. NOTE 2 (personal): When the square bollard features 1 bolt, this bolt will be in the middle of the square. When the square bollard features 2 bolts, these bolts will be at the top and at the bottom of the reflector.

metas.name: North Carolina - Street signs with letters (SR) and arrows
metas.note: North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers (SR) and arrows in addition to the street name. They tend to appear at intersections with other SR roads, but can also be installed elsewhere. If the arrow is missing, I would still trust this meta. The so called Secondary Road system is still unique to this state. Do not confuse it with a similar Pennsylvania meta, tho (in Pennsylvania, SR stands for State Route). Road numbers following SR are sometimes marked on the map with a rectangular number tag and can help with pinpointing.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: North Carolina - Unique State Route Signage

Road numbers following SR are sometimes marked on the map with a rectangular number tag and can help with pinpointing.

metas.name: Texas - Grainy Road (salt and pepper)
metas.note: One of the most famous meta in the USA has to be the salt and pepper pavement in Texas. Its name referes to the grainy texture of the road in that state. Apart from knowing this, be aware that Illinois can use the same pavement as Texas does, but Texas preferes to use this pavement than anything else. Differenciate these two regions by simply looking around and using the landscape.

The Utah variant usually has two bolts.
